summaryPoints: Bangladesh built a commanding first-innings platform of 522/7, spearheaded by Mushfiqur Rahim's brilliant 219.

summaryTab.matchCommentary:
The Test match at Shere Bangla National Stadium commenced with high tactical intensity as Bangladesh posted 522/7 (159.6 ov) in their opening innings. In response, Zimbabwe countered with 304/9 (105.3 ov), setting the stage for a compelling contest of tactical endurance. Early sessions tested batting resolve against disciplined seam movement, with both attacks striving to gain the upper hand on a developing surface.

The defining turning point arrived during 6-Wicket Spell: Mehidy Miraz (6/38), which irrevocably altered the trajectory of the match. As the match progressed through its pivotal middle stages, Mehidy Miraz delivered a masterclass for Bangladesh (95 Runs & 9 Wkts), absorbing intense pressure and tilting the momentum decisively. Crucial partnership stands and incisive bowling spells broke the opposition's resistance, shifting the control share (Bangladesh 61%) and allowing Bangladesh to dictate terms heading into the decisive sessions.

Entering the final innings, Zimbabwe faced an uphill battle under unrelenting scoreboard pressure. Bangladesh's bowling unit, bolstered by Mushfiqur Rahim (226 Runs), maintained relentless discipline and attacked the stumps relentlessly. Wicket clusters in the closing sessions dismantled any remaining resistance, sealing Bangladesh won by 218 runs in comprehensive fashion.

Verdict: Bangladesh's triumph was built on superior pressure absorption, clinical execution during critical moments, and the ability to dominate key sessions. While Zimbabwe produced fighting phases, Bangladesh won the pivotal turning points and sustained higher tactical control across all five days to emerge as deserved victors.
